newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Assmang H1 year taxed profit falls 15 pct.
newsitem.headline: Assmang H1 year taxed profit falls 15 pct.

text.p: Anglovaal Minerals Ltd unit Associated Manganese Mines of South Africa Ltd said on Thursday group profit for the six months to December 31 fell to 67.1 million rand from 78.8 million rand previously.
It said the slump in earnings came after manganese ore sales fell 27 percent to 448,355 tons as a result of weaker market conditions and the timing of shipments.
Sales volumes were expected to remain at lower levels for the rest of the current financial year, it added.
After transfers to non-distributable reserves, group earnings declined to 38.3 million rands from 69.8 million rands, Assmang said.
It proposed an unchanged interim dividend of 250 cents a share.
Capital expenditure at the group's mines increased to 28.8 million rand from nine million rand.

The group said capital expenditure at its mines was planned at 30 million rand for the rest of the year and would be spent mainly on ongoing projects including underground development, mining and metallurgical equipment and the replacement of heavy duty vehicles.
Results of the group's wholly-owned subsidiary Feralloys Ltd reflected a drop in operating profit to 11.3 million rand from 40.1 million rand, Assmang said.
It said the sales of ferro-manganese remained stable at 75,000 tons from 78,000 tons but dollar prices had fallen.
"The weaker rand has to some extent offset the lower prices," Assmang said.
Capital expenditure at Feralloys for the half-year to June 31 1997 was estimated at 75 million rand.
Assmang is jointly controlled by Avmin Ltd and The Associated Ore and Metal Corporation Ltd.
